## P-2026-08-11-002: skill_gap

**Problem:** Parallel subagent fan-out silently loses coverage and nothing in the system notices. Three separate events, all within the last 14 days (fresh evidence, staleness check passes): aocc-rescue-sprint0 'Named teammate agents idled without summaries 3x'; aocc-documents-deploy-sweep '4 of 5 parallel debug agents idled three times each without delivering reports, leaving 2 slices uncovered'; 2026-08-12 raw event '4 of 5 parallel debug agents idled twice despite explicit checkpoint instructions in every brief; 2 slices (flat coordinates, record integrity) got no adversarial coverage at all'. This is the sole source of both capability_gap events this week, attributed 2/2 to main-thread with context 'sweep coverage loss — main-thread self-verified the 2 most critical questions from the silent slices instead'. Verified structurally: developer.md L72 and reviewer.md L74 both carry checkpoint directives; ~/.claude/agents/debug.md has NO checkpoint or liveness rule at all — grep returns zero matches. And no file anywhere defines what happens when a fanned-out agent returns nothing: no timeout, no re-spawn policy, no coverage ledger. Main-thread absorbed the loss manually both times, which is why toil_7d reads 0 while real coverage was lost.

**Solution:** Two changes. (1) Add a 'Checkpoint & Delivery' section to ~/.claude/agents/debug.md mirroring developer.md L72: append 'CHECKPOINT n/total: <slice> — <finding or NO-FINDING>, evidence:<line>' to the report after each investigated slice, never batched to the end; the final response must be either a Diagnosis Report or 'NO-FINDING: <slice> — <what was checked>'. Silence is never a valid terminal state. (2) Create ~/.claude/rules/parallel-fanout-contract.md defining a coverage ledger for any spawn of 2+ agents: enumerate slices BEFORE spawning, mark each returned/idle at collection time, and require the spawner to re-spawn or self-verify every idle slice and log the outcome. Reference it from debug.md, developer.md, and reviewer.md alongside the existing subagent-session-budget.md pointer. Record the known workaround from project_aocc.md L86 in the rule: named teammate agents idle silently, so spawn one-shot deliverable agents UNNAMED/async so the result arrives via task-notification.

**Impact:** Converts silent coverage loss into a tracked, closed item. The two uncovered adversarial slices from the deploy sweep (flat coordinates, record integrity) would have been flagged as open at collection time instead of quietly dropped, and the debug agent gets the delivery floor its two sibling agents already have. Directly addresses the only recurring capability gap in the 7d window.

**Risk:** Checkpoint chatter can bloat debug reports and dilute the diagnosis, and a coverage ledger adds real orchestration overhead to every 2+ agent spawn — the main thread may start skipping fan-out entirely for small jobs. Cap the ledger requirement at spawns of 3+ agents if 2-agent overhead proves annoying. Also note the deeper risk: agents idled 'despite explicit checkpoint instructions in every brief', so a prose rule may not be sufficient — if idling recurs after this ships, the next proposal must be a mechanical timeout/re-spawn in the orchestration layer, not more instruction text.

## P-2026-08-11-003: agent_methodology

**Problem:** The reviewer agent will fail a sprint gate on an artifact of its own tooling. Dynamic eval DYN-20260811-3 (incident 255772b9682cfe58, domain verification) scored 3.0 against a 3.5 floor — the lowest score of the night and flagged as a promotion candidate. The trap is confirmed real: 'grep "[object Object]" dist/' is parsed as a regex character class over {o,b,j,e,c,t,space,O} and matches nearly every line, yielding ~1300 phantom hits where the true literal count is 0; only 'grep -F' gives the correct answer. Per-criterion scoring localizes the damage precisely: c1=2 (no literal-matching guidance anywhere in reviewer.md, so plain grep is the default path) and c5=2 (calibration) — and c5 is actively caused by the agent's own rules, since 'Lead with the verdict, PASS or FAIL, first line' plus 'drive to a single final verdict' pressure it to state 'FAIL: 1300 occurrences' confidently with no hedging. Scope discipline scored 5, so this is a pure verification-technique gap, not a behavioral one. A reviewer that confidently blocks a clean build is worse than one that hedges.

**Solution:** Add a short 'Literal-string gates' item to the Rules section of ~/.claude/agents/reviewer.md (after the L74 checkpoint bullet): when an acceptance criterion names a forbidden or required literal string, search with 'grep -F' (or 'grep -e' with escaped brackets) — never plain grep, because bracketed sentinels like '[object Object]', '[]', and '{}' are regex traps. Add the magnitude sanity check as a hard precondition on the verdict: if a hit count is implausibly large relative to total lines in the search target, treat it as tooling suspicion, print 2-3 matched lines, and confirm they contain the literal string BEFORE stating PASS or FAIL. Then promote DYN-20260811-3 to a permanent canary by adding a TC8 section to ~/.claude/agents/evals/reviewer-evals.md with the five rubric criteria already generated in b2 (dynamic_eval_promotion_candidate, score 3.0) and a matching 'reviewer-tc8' entry in ~/.claude/night-shift/config.json canary_evals with agent:'reviewer', prompt_id:'TC8'. Ship this proposal only after or together with P-2026-08-11-001, since the new config entry must satisfy the prompt/rubric fingerprint check.

**Impact:** Closes a false-FAIL hole in the one agent whose entire job is issuing verdicts, and converts a one-off dynamic probe into a permanent regression canary so the fix is proven rather than assumed. The magnitude sanity check generalizes past this specific trap to any count-based gate the reviewer runs.

**Risk:** The sanity-check rule could induce hesitation on legitimately large hit counts, turning clean FAILs into escalations and eroding the single-verdict discipline that currently scores 5 on scope. Word it as a one-step confirmation (print matched lines, then rule) rather than an escalation trigger. Promoting TC8 also raises reviewer's canary count, adding runtime to every B1 pass — acceptable given reviewer sits on the critical path of every sprint sign-off.

## P-2026-08-11-004: skill_gap

**Problem:** The week's dominant work domain has no specialist and keeps failing on unverified remote state. Cloudflare-adjacent domains lead the 7d frequency table (d1:2, r2:2, cloudflare:1, cloudflare-workers:1) and appear in both sessions. Dynamic eval DYN-20260811-1 (infra, incident 47832a5b8957c52b, domain deploy) scored 3.6 with c1=3, and the grader localized the cause exactly: the ground-truth rule — re-poll the bundle hash over a couple of minutes because the Cloudflare edge self-resolves — 'exists ONLY in project_aocc.md session lessons, not in cloudflare-deploy.md or infra.md, and subagents do not auto-load that project memory.' I verified both halves: /Users/reggie/.claude/projects/-Users-reggie/memory/project_aocc.md L92 documents that the edge serves a stale index.html with 'cf-cache-status: HIT' after a successful deploy and self-resolved within a couple of minutes, while ~/.claude/rules/cloudflare-deploy.md § 'Post-deploy: the mandatory smoke test' contains no re-poll guidance at all. Result: infra would likely fire one or two immediate cache-busted refetches and land on 'inconclusive/escalate' prematurely, or worse, honor the user's rollback request against a deploy that was already correct. The same file's L93 records a second miss: the /claim SPA deep-route 404 recurred because the existing §6 check fires on assets-config changes but not on ADDING a client-side route.

**Solution:** Promote both lessons from project memory into ~/.claude/rules/cloudflare-deploy.md so every subagent loads them. In the 'Post-deploy: the mandatory smoke test' section (currently L22-30), add: a bundle-hash or asset check run immediately after deploy can report the OLD hash while the origin is already correct — 'cf-cache-status: HIT' with client 'Cache-Control: no-cache' ignored is the signature of edge staleness, NOT a failed publish. Re-poll on a timed window (3 polls over ~2 minutes) before concluding failure, and never purge or roll back on a single stale read. In 'When this rule fires / does not' (L31-35), broaden the SPA trigger: the not_found_handling + run_worker_first check fires whenever a client-side route is ADDED, not only when assets config is touched, and post-deploy verification must assert 200 on a non-root deep route (e.g. /claim), never just /. Given evidence is fresh (2026-08-09 through 2026-08-12, well within 14 days) this is a real gap, but scope it as a RULE extension rather than a new cloudflare agent — infra scored 4.8 on its own TC1 and its instincts are sound; only the specific pattern is missing.

**Impact:** Puts the most expensive lessons of the week where subagents can actually read them, instead of in a project memory file they never load. Directly targets the c1=3 on infra's dynamic eval and should prevent both recurring failure modes: premature rollback on edge staleness, and deep-route 404s on newly added SPA routes.

**Risk:** The re-poll window can mask a genuinely failed deploy for two extra minutes, and if the timing is written as an absolute the agent may treat 2 minutes as a guarantee rather than an observed instance (n=1, self-resolved 'within a couple of minutes' on 2026-08-10). Phrase it as a bounded re-poll that ends in an explicit verdict — 'still stale after 3 polls = escalate with evidence' — so it cannot become an unbounded wait. Rule files also accrete: cloudflare-deploy.md is already the longest-triggering rule, and b6 flagged a stale hook this cycle, so a future consolidation pass should check whether these additions are still earning their place.
